text:
maria (infra): FYI, after last night's GPU driver push we're seeing NCCL errors across Dedicated and two Private customers that opted into auto-upgrade. lots of NCCL WARN / NCCL_ABORTED on allreduce.

sanjay (runtime): Can you paste the dmesg + nvidia-smi from one of the failing nodes? My suspicion is driver/CUDA/NCCL mismatch or kernel module ABI change.

maria (infra): Copying snippets from node-gpu-12:
```
$ nvidia-smi
Driver Version: 535.86.10  CUDA Version: 12.1
...
$ dmesg | tail -n 20
[  +1.234567] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: Failed to initialize X driver
[  +1.234568] kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing
[  +1.234569] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000...
[  +1.234570] NCCL WARN Call to something: NCCL_ABORTED
```

eli (cust-succ): One of the affected customers (finance-priv) reported they also saw an internal OS security patch earlier this week — their infra team did a kernel update and we think DKMS modules weren't rebuilt.

kate (security): That lines up. If DKMS didn't rebuild after kernel update, the nvidia module will mismatch. Also the support matrix we've been using (v5.0 doc) requires pinned driver ranges for Private installs; but customers keep asking we support 'latest' in private.

sanjay (runtime): Current rollout target was driver 535 + CUDA 12.1 + NCCL 2.18. That combo works on our cloud images (kernel 5.15+). But a few on-prem nodes are stuck on older kernels (5.4/4.19) or have vendor kernels with different module signing policies. The regression likely from a kernel ABI incompatibility.

maria (infra): Quick triage notes:
- Hosted/Dedicated: majority stable, but we pushed 535 to all Dedicated pools last night for perf wins; rolling back single pool improved error rate.
- Private: customers with auto-upgrade saw failures if their nodes had kernel mismatches.

deploy-bot: Canary alert: dedicated-pool-7 failure rate +12% in 30m; rollback recommended.

sanjay (runtime): Immediate mitigations:
1) Roll back Dedicated pools to 525 (we kept the package in apt repo) to stop the outage.
2) For Private customers, we can't force a rollback, but we should push an advisory and a preflight agent that checks kernel, driver, dkms status, and NCCL version.

maria (infra): Rollback command used on the pool (example):
```
# on control plane
kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets
ssh node-gpu-12 'sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-525 && sudo reboot'
kubectl uncordon node-gpu-12
```
Rollback reduced NCCL aborts in Dedicated pools to baseline within ~15m.

eli (cust-succ): Customer asks: why did auto-upgrade break things? They explicitly opted into 'auto-update drivers' in the private console. They want either stronger guarantees or an opt-out.

kate (security): We need to update the Private/VPC install docs and contracts: explicitly call out supported kernel/driver matrix and that auto-upgrade requires DKMS-compatible kernels or operator-managed node images. Also add a checkbox in the console for "I confirm nodes use supported kernels/DKMS".

sanjay (runtime): Proposal for longer-term:
- Add a preflight/daemon that runs on Private installs and reports back: uname -r, modinfo nvidia | grep version, ldconfig -p | grep libcudart, and nccl tests.
- If mismatch detected, auto-disable auto-upgrade and open a support ticket. Provide a one-click 'rebuild DKMS' helper script for common distros.

maria (infra): Also need an operations policy for our Dedicated rollouts: don't push drivers that require kernel ABI > target kernel across pools. Add kernel detection to canary logic.

ops-bot: Action created: INFRA-1422 "Private preflight agent and console upgrades" assigned to infra-team, priority P1.

eli (cust-succ): For affected customers I'm sending an advisory template now with recommended steps and a temporary workaround (route inference to hosted region or paused autoscaling for affected nodes).

maria (infra): Question for product/security: do we want to expand our supported matrix so Private can request 'latest' drivers but we only enable when kernel >= X and DKMS present? Or should Private always pin to a certified combo?

kate (security): We should require pinning by default for Private. Allow 'latest' only if preflight gate passes and customer explicitly opts in with acceptance of risk SLA. That keeps compliance and reduces surprise.

sanjay (runtime): Technical note: we could also ship a small user-space fallback that avoids NCCL collectives when kernel modules are broken — fall back to gloo-like algorithms or split across CPU for small workloads — but that's a stopgap and will increase latency/cost.

maria (infra): Next steps I've assigned:
- rollback Dedicated pools fully to 525 (done)
- ship advisory and hotfix script for Private (eli)
- schedule RFC to update installer to include preflight checks and opt-in gating (sanjay + infra + product)

eli (cust-succ): I'll also ask the affected customers to run this quick diagnostic one-liner and share results:
```
curl -sS https://our-agent/check | sudo sh
# outputs: kernel, driver, dkms status, nccl version
```

sanjay (runtime): Thx. Once we get diagnostics from the two affected Private installs we can recommend either DKMS rebuild (sudo dkms autoinstall) or the older driver. Long-term we should log driver/kernel versions to the console for Private so customers can see drift.

maria (infra): thanks all — good catch. I'll follow up with a postmortem and a checklist for future driver rollouts. :thumbsup
